title: The Father does not receive acquired glory
english: But the Father does not receive acquired glory, for he is perfect, infinite, incomprehensible, and without need of beauty or seemliness.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The author is beginning his explanation of why acquired glory is not fitting for the Father, stating the first reason in a series that will also cover the Word and the man of Christ.

title: The Word does not receive acquired glory; the man of Christ does
english: Nor does the Word receive it, for he is God begotten from the Father, through whom angels and heavens and the boundless magnitudes of earth and all the materials and compositions of created things together have come to be. Rather, it is the man of Christ who, being raised from the dead, is exalted and glorified, while his enemies
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius continues his argument about who receives acquired glory, now turning from the Father to the Word and then to the man of Christ.

title: Shame of enemies and scattering by the Word's raising of his temple
english: openly took up shame. But those who, out of envy, took up hatred against him and were fenced in by a hostile battle-line are scattered, since the Word and God fittingly raised his own temple.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is closing his argument that acquired glory belongs to the man of Christ, not to the Father or the Word, and now describes the fate of Christ's enemies.
